macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin slips below $64K as weak stablecoin inflows signal softer demand
items.summary: Bitcoin fell about 2.3% over 24 hours and traded near $63,919, with broader crypto markets also lower. The move came alongside weakening stablecoin inflows and ongoing uncertainty around U.S. market structure legislation.

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs see $240 million in outflows, led by BlackRock’s IBIT
items.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $240 million in net outflows, with BlackRock’s IBIT accounting for $212 million of the withdrawals. The flows add to recent pressure on Bitcoin and ETF demand.

items.title: Coinbase reshuffles senior leadership ahead of key legal and regulatory battles
items.summary: Coinbase announced leadership changes, including departures in legal, HR, and Base-related roles. The move comes as the exchange faces heightened scrutiny and a crucial CLARITY Act vote.

items.title: CLARITY Act passage odds cut as Senate vote concerns grow
items.summary: Galaxy Research lowered the odds of the U.S. CLARITY Act passing in 2026 to 30% amid concerns about Senate support. The bill remains a key market-structure proposal for digital assets, stablecoin rewards, and DeFi rules.

items.title: Bitcoin climbs above $63K as easing oil prices lift risk appetite
items.summary: Crypto.news reported Bitcoin trading above $63,000 as falling oil prices improved risk sentiment. The broader market remained mixed, but Bitcoin showed relative resilience compared with some altcoins.

items.title: Hong Kong SFC forces crypto platforms to drop SMS authentication
items.summary: Hong Kong’s securities regulator ordered crypto platforms to phase out SMS-based authentication, reflecting tighter operational security requirements. The rule change is part of a broader push to harden digital-asset platform safeguards.

items.title: XRP sees price pressure even as Ripple expands institutional RLUSD tools
items.summary: XRP was down slightly over 24 hours and saw heavy long liquidations, while Ripple launched Ripple Mint to help institutions mint, redeem, and manage RLUSD. The development underscores continued product expansion around Ripple’s stablecoin ecosystem.

items.title: Bitdeer unveils $36 million Nevada factory to expand Bitcoin mining
items.summary: Bitdeer announced a new $36 million factory in Nevada aimed at strengthening its Bitcoin mining operations. The project adds to continued infrastructure investment in the mining sector.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Work for cross-app task automation
items.summary: OpenAI unveiled ChatGPT Work, an agent designed to gather context across apps and files and create documents on Mac and Windows, signaling a push deeper into workplace automation. The release intensifies competition in professional AI tools.

items.title: OpenAI releases GPT-Live, a real-time voice model family
items.summary: OpenAI launched GPT-Live, a new family of voice models that can listen and speak simultaneously in real time. The rollout extends to multiple consumer tiers and highlights rapid progress in conversational AI.

items.title: Meta opens developer access to Muse Spark and upgrades the model
items.summary: Meta released long-awaited developer access to its Muse Spark AI model and introduced an upgraded version. The move positions Meta more directly against Anthropic and OpenAI in paid model access.

items.title: Meta plans in-house AI chip manufacturing starting in September
items.summary: Reuters reported that Meta plans to begin manufacturing an artificial intelligence chip in September, according to an internal memo. The effort is part of its broader plan to expand computing capacity for AI workloads.

items.title: Micron announces more than $250 billion U.S. investment through 2035
items.summary: Micron said it plans to invest over $250 billion in the United States through 2035, citing surging AI-driven demand for memory chips. The announcement underscores how AI continues to reshape semiconductor investment.

items.title: SpaceXAI launches Grok 4.5 for coding and agentic tasks
items.summary: SpaceXAI launched the Grok 4.5 model, describing it as its most intelligent model to date and targeting coding and agentic tasks. The release adds to the fast pace of frontier model competition.

items.title: Anthropic appoints Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust
items.summary: Anthropic named former U.S. Federal Reserve chair Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust, the oversight body charged with keeping the company aligned with its public mission. The appointment is part of Anthropic’s governance and safety positioning.

items.title: Google, Meta, OpenAI and others continue intensifying AI infrastructure race
items.summary: Recent coverage points to a broader industry trend of soaring compute investment, new data center builds, and custom chips as major AI companies race to expand capacity. The pattern reflects how infrastructure has become central to model development and deployment.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: IO Interactive to close one studio after Xbox pulls funding from project
items.summary: IO Interactive, the studio behind Hitman and 007: First Light, will shut down one of its studios and lay off staff after Xbox withdrew funding for an upcoming project. The move adds to a turbulent period for game development and publishing tied to platform-holder investment decisions.

items.title: Xbox Game Pass growth reportedly fell short of Microsoft’s targets
items.summary: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma reportedly acknowledged that Game Pass has not grown as Microsoft expected, with reports saying the service is tens of millions of subscribers short of earlier targets. The update highlights ongoing pressure on Microsoft’s subscription strategy.

items.title: Sony’s move away from physical PlayStation discs sparks backlash
items.summary: Sony’s decision to end physical discs on PlayStation consoles continues to draw criticism, with its first related tweet facing a negative response. The issue has also fueled a growing consumer petition opposing the shift to digital-only releases.

items.title: Double Fine and Compulsion Games reportedly going independent
items.summary: Reports say Double Fine and Compulsion Games are becoming independent as part of a broader restructuring tied to Microsoft’s gaming business. The same reporting also says Microsoft is selling Ninja Theory and Undead Labs.

items.title: Xbox layoffs reportedly hit id Software and Obsidian
items.summary: VGC reports that Microsoft’s latest cuts may have significantly affected id Software’s coding team and reduced staff at Obsidian by 60 to 70 developers. The scale of the layoffs suggests broader cost-cutting across Xbox’s first-party operations.

items.title: IO confirms Project Fantasy will continue independently
items.summary: VGC reports that IO Interactive has confirmed Project Fantasy will keep moving forward independently after the split with Xbox. The project remains in development despite the funding change.

items.title: WayForward announces next Shantae game
items.summary: WayForward revealed a new Shantae game at Anime Expo and gave it a 2027 release window. The announcement adds another long-running indie franchise entry to the pipeline.

items.title: Nintendo of Europe to stop selling the Nintendo Switch in 2027
items.summary: VGC reports that Nintendo of Europe will end sales of the original Switch on its store in February 2027. The report also says Nintendo has confirmed a Switch 2 revision with replaceable batteries in Europe to meet new EU rules.

items.title: Pokémon Go marks its 10th anniversary with live event coverage
items.summary: IGN is covering Pokémon Go’s 10th anniversary livestream, where Niantic is expected to make live announcements and reveal surprises. The event is one of the day’s biggest mobile-game moments.

items.title: Call of Duty: Black Ops 1 and 2 ports release on PS4 and PS5
items.summary: IGN reports that Call of Duty: Black Ops 1 and 2 are now available on PS4 and PS5. The launch gives PlayStation players access to two classic entries, though the price point has drawn attention.

items.title: Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced sees strong Steam launch
items.summary: IGN says Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced has reached around 100,000 concurrent players on Steam, giving it the series’ biggest Steam peak so far. The result points to continued interest in the franchise’s older entries.

items.title: GTA Online’s next major update set for next week
items.summary: IGN reports that GTA Online’s Kortz Center Heist update will release next week. Fans have already spotted multiple Rockstar-related Easter eggs tied to the new content.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Swift launches blockchain-based shared ledger for round-the-clock payments
items.summary: Swift unveiled a blockchain-based shared ledger with 16 banks, including Citi and HSBC, to support 24/7 cross-border payments and compete with stablecoin-based systems.

items.title: India removes import duty on some electronics and smartphone parts
items.summary: India scrapped import duties on certain mobile phone and electronics components, a move that could lower costs for manufacturers such as Apple and Xiaomi.

items.title: Apple and Broadcom expand chip supply agreement
items.summary: Apple said it will spend more than $30 billion under a chip-supply deal with Broadcom, which also includes an expansion of a factory in Colorado.

items.title: Meta to begin manufacturing an AI chip in September
items.summary: Reuters reported that Meta plans to start manufacturing its own AI chip from September as part of a broader effort to expand computing capacity.

items.title: Meta launches in-house smart glasses
items.summary: Meta introduced a new line of smart glasses designed in-house, signaling a deeper push into wearable technology.

items.title: Microsoft cuts nearly 5,000 jobs, mostly in Xbox
items.summary: Microsoft announced a major layoff round affecting about 5,000 workers, with most cuts concentrated in its Xbox division as it restructures the business.

items.title: EU advances proposal to allow scanning for child sexual abuse material
items.summary: EU lawmakers backed a measure to revive temporary rules that would let online platforms detect and remove child sexual abuse material, with debate continuing over privacy and end-to-end encryption.

items.title: SpaceX launches Starship in first test flight since IPO
items.summary: SpaceX launched its Starship rocket in its first test flight since going public, marking another major milestone in the company’s launch program.
